OriginalEnglish: Grinning bright-blue blobs beloved for their wide eyes and wobbly bodies. Get oozed to them<MV>they're goobiquitous.
Though these quivering jellies are known to cower from the sun's heat, they aren't wholly lacking in backbone.
Bat-like blighters with grins as cheeky as they are toothy. If you value your blood, steer clear of these sneaky suckers.
Despite their obscure origins in a dark domain, they're kindly characters, always happy to heal the hurt.
Creepy corpses made to move by the sinister spooks inside them. Beware the foetid fluids they fling<FG>
Being dead, these creatures don't know when they're beaten, and won't rest in peace until they're left in pieces.
These vulture-snake hybrids store up searing flames in their lungs, and spew them forth at foes when fighting.
They have a deep-seated dislike of the cold, and some say their wings possess a peculiar power...
These infant fiends may look cute, but don't fall for their butter-wouldn't-melt act<MV>those forks aren't for eating with<FG>
It'll be a few years before these diminutive demons have enough MP to cast Kaboom, but that doesn't stop them trying.
Their heavy hammers mostly miss their mark, but when they hit home, they pack a proper punch. Beware<FG>
Some suspect them of being aspiring comics, and that all their slapstick swinging is actually an act.
Armour animated by the souls of slain swordsmen. Their skill with sword and shield was honed over countless clashes.
They share a rich rapport with healslimes, whose reparatory powers they rely upon in the all-consuming chaos of combat.
Kindly creatures who instantly attend to allies' ailments, even when their own wounds are worse.
Their bulbous blue bodies are similar to standard slimes, but they float as if by magic, tentacles trailing in the wind.
Craggy creatures concealed among rocks who explode when endangered, taking flocks of foes down with them.
Pacifists at heart, they like nothing more than to doze in quiet corners. Disturb their dreams at your peril<FG>
Having somehow gained sentience, these jangling gems drive opponents potty with a pouchful of painful pranks.
Their habit of flashing their booty has earned them ample attention among avaricious adventurers.
Ex-employees of an ancient emperor who were interred alongside him so they could serve in the afterlife.
They're insanely envious of the living, and delight in depriving others of the gift of life.
Automatons formed of earth by monstrous mitts, they forgo spells and weapons for old-fashioned fisticuffs.
They barely seem to flinch at regular attacks...and then drop to the dirt in a defeated pile of dust.
Murderous mechanoids programmed for one purpose<MV>to exterminate any and all enemies on sight.
Their internal power plant will provide energy indefinitely, but their red eye requires regular bulb changes.
Don't be fooled by their fluffy fur and funny faces<MV>these big-beaked bad 'uns pack a punch<FG>
One whack from their long, white tails can set enemies snoring<MV>and sometimes even bring about the Big Sleep.
Forget regular slimes<MV>these blighters ooze strength from every pore. Eight of them goonite to form a king slime.
For all their might, they like merging more than mauling, and seek like-minded slimes for consensual conglomeration.
The striped coats of these frost-flinging felines make it look like they've just escaped from the slammer.
Some wonder if it's their fur that's stripy or the skin underneath, but no one can get close enough to check...
A long-suffering servant of Robbin' 'Ood, who manages to stay merry despite his master's domineering manner.
As a token of his undeclared devotion, Robbin' neglects his own wardrobe to garb his guardians in golden armour.
These wary warriors stay well away from the action, preferring to fire on their foes from afar.
The other bodkins constantly belittle their basic bow skills, so they vent their resentment on passing adventurers.
Stupidly strong and, well, stupid swingers whose colossal clubs will leave you seeing stars if struck.
Since swallowing a story about saliva's attack-boosting properties, they've licked their clubs with gusto.
Benevolent blobs who ooze their majestic mass to make pancakes out of the enemies of slimekind.
Formed when eight like-minded slimes become one. If stripped of their crown, they swiftly goo their separate ways.
Despite their ponderous appearance, these green-clad sirs slash with surprising and sustained celerity.
With memories of their past lord fading, they challenge worthy warriors to fill the void in their hollow hearts.
Reptilian rogues who like nothing more than to flambé foes with blazing breath and then cut them into cubes.
They're known to admire enemies deft enough to defeat them, and are often found fighting for former foes.
Sculptures that slowly gained sentience. Their stony skin is unsusceptible to all but the strongest strikes.
They hide amongst statues and wait for prey, sometimes turning back to stone after too long spent stationary.
Stalwart sentinels of the underworld whose myriad moves include foiling foes with Fizzle and swooping strikes.
They're so self-conscious about their gravelly growl that they collect rainwater to gargoyle with before bedtime.
Pesky puddles whose liquid metal bodies bounce blows right off them...should they stay long enough to be struck.
The burnished bubbles which bob above their silver surface serve as painful projectiles when pressed.
Bedevilled boxes who lie in wait for daydreaming dupes, and mangle them with murderous maws and killer curses.
Sinister spooks seduced by all things booty-ful stow away inside them, their eyes glistening with glee.
One-eyed mountains of muscle who leave ruin in their wake. Powerless only in the face of their own unruly urges.
Their clubs can break boulders, so be sure to stay out of sight. Failing that, give them an eyeful<FG>
Trident-toting terrors who flatten foes with mighty magic before bringing their bestial brawn to bear.
Rumour has it that minidemons turn into archdemons with age. They certainly share some striking similarities...
Stylish in sumptuous silver coats, these devious demons bound about the battlefield, slinging spells as they go.
No trinket escapes the eye of these crazed collectors. Lock up your valuables<FG>
They rile prey by running rings round them. Once their claws have found a target, it's no more Mr Nice Kitty.
These grown-up great sabrecubs are fearsome yet faithful felines, bearing buddies into battle upon their broad backs.
Bound by unbreakable bonds, these stout sirs and their slimy steeds are truly loyal, healing without hesitation.
Having pledged to protect the puny, they goo to great lengths to keep their mates and their mounts safe from harm.
Mucky mitts who lurk in the earth, ready to pounce on passers-by. Bash them before they beckon for backup<FG>
Those who've uprooted them insist there's nothing below the wrist. Others tell them to ‘pull the other one’.
The prodigious proportions of these highly evolved versions of the rockbomb prohibit people from passing.
Try as they might, no one can work out why they're always so stony-faced and quarry-some.
Mischievous spirits who can mimic other monsters down to the minutest detail<MV>even matching their martial might.
And it's not just monsters they copy<MV>they take on human form and play tricks on townsfolk too<FG>
These fun-loving phantoms like nothing more than flying into adventurers' faces and shouting ‘boo<FG>’
Bags o' laughs often ask them to come up with jokes for their comedy routines<MV>they're the original ghost writers<FG>
One look at the weird way they waggle their limbs can make even the dourest of warriors want to dance along.
The mud they're made from is imbued with magic<MV>rub your face with it, and your skin will be silky smooth in no time<FG>
Sinister statues carved from ice and animated with arcane energies. They're colder than stone, and twice as tough.
They guard the entrance to Mt Neverest, but secretly wish they could be stationed somewhere a bit more balmy.
A monster masquerading as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills, blasting passers-by with thunderbolts.
When the wind picks up, they get blown off over the horizon, and have to fly for miles to find their way home.
Machines made to murder metal slimes. Despite their fulsome frames, they pursue prey with spellbinding speed.
Steely in spirit and substance, these automated assassins will stop at nothing to see their mercurial marks melted down.
Magically mutated chimaeras who soar through the skies, slinging spells from on high to flummox foes below.
Their wings change colour when they evolve, making their plumage prized property among poachers.
This axe-wielding outlaw is all mouth and no trousers<MV>when his victims turn violent, he begs for forgiveness.
His customary costume doesn't leave a lot to the imagination. As far as Robbin's concerned, if you've got it, flaunt it<FG>
Eye-catching orange slimes who seek to outgoo their more popular blue cousins through rigorous training.
Some say their conspicuous colour confirms they're girls, while others maintain it's due to all the red meat they eat.
Some say these fiery phantasms are the souls of the damned, burning with hatred for humankind.
They try to put a brave face on their unhappy fate, and get very upset if anyone suggests their smiles are just for show.
The experience of eliminating one of these metal monarchs is certain to supplement any adventurer's advancement.
They flee from foes with surprising speed for their size, counter-attacking on occasion for kingly effect.
They prefer patching up pals to pugilism. Even healslimes are in awe of their prodigious palliative powers.
So hardwired is their healing impulse that they have to resist the urge to fix foes, who often off them first in any case.
Sentries of stone enlivened by evil enchantments whose fearsome fists pack an incomparably potent punch.
They trail targets tirelessly, trampling over anyone and anything in their path without a second thought.
High-born rug rats of demonic descent who use their childish charm to approach prey, then fry it with Frizzle.
Trickier tykes than accident- prone imps, and walking proof of the difference an elite education can make.
Battle-worn warriors in life, now they're content to shamble about leaving poisonous puddles in their wake.
Their HP is as high as their IQ is low, and they seem to lash out at approaching foes more out of instinct than intent.
Kindly creatures that sacrifice themselves in a flash to aid comrades caught between a rock and a hard place.
They can live happily for millennia without so much as a murmur, but if provoked, they kick off with Kerplunk.
Axe-wielding dragons who strike swiftly and strongly, flambéing foes left uncleft with burning breath.
They've been known to wield an iron mallet, but seem most relaxed with an axe. Perhaps it's a sentimental thing<FH>
Incorporeal creatures born from the deepest darkness, who silently stalk their prey before suddenly striking.
They dwell in the darkness and shun the sun, but are oddly attracted to bright and breezy personalities.
Free-flying fowl who like to ruffle feathers with Woosh before dealing damage with skilful swordsmanship.
Despite being magic maestros, they're let down by fits of forgetfulness<MV>a product of their pea-sized brains.
Hairy horrors hailing from the frozen north. They love licking unlucky adventurers with their long, lolling tongues.
Their sensitive tongues can taste prey from far away, so they know when an appetising adventurer is approaching.
As eager adventurers ache to earn experience from splatting them, these quicksilver slimes are loath to loiter.
Bolder specimens scoff at beating a retreat, flinging Frizz at foes while stiffening their steely skins.
Slimy sovereigns straining at the seams with medicinal magic. They use Omniheal to aid ailing allies.
Bottomless founts of MP whose bodies balloon to ever more majestic magnitudes as their magic amasses.
Jolly jellyfish who congregate with their kinsmonsters at the water's edge.
They send foes to sleep, then dither dreamily until the next chance to strike.
Defeating these gilded gladiators yields a royal ransom in riches, but is the risk really worth the reward<FH>
Far from as good as gold, they fling their fists around furiously with nary a care for their surroundings.
Sentient suits of armour forged in the fires of the underworld. Often accompanied by cureslime comrades.
Legend has it that the once-white armour of these fury-fuelled fiends was stained with sanguine spatterings.
An intrepid explorer who met his maker in a septic swamp. He vomits venom at victims to spread his infection.
From corrosive catarrh to mould-breeding mucus, this foetid fellow has a secretion for every occasion.
Pestilent puddles whose touch is toxic, which makes forging firm friendships unfeasible.
They become markedly less bubbly when tired, and ooze off to the nearest swamp for a poisonous pick-me-up.
Dastardly drackies who cause chaos with Kasnooze before dealing dozing foes the mother of all rude awakenings.
According to experts, Kasnooze is actually a lullaby drackymas use to send their little ones to sleep.
Treacherous chests who wait for wondering wanderers to lift their lids, then show them the cost of curiosity.
Treasure hunters who've met these bestial boxes speak of their struggles with PTCD<FI> Post-Traumatic Chest Disorder.
Playful pouches of peril whose unshakeable smiles are almost as disturbing as their dancing.
They crack up at their own gags, oblivious to the glares of nearby hammerhoods<MV>the true comedy connoisseurs.
A legendary one-eyed giant famed for flattening fortresses with the ease of a toddler toppling a toy tower.
It once served an evil priest with Belial and Pazuzu. Though undeniably mighty, it's not without its weak points.
Trees that have taken on lives of their own, and turned to ambushing adventurers who wander into the woods.
These once-docile woods creatures were driven to distraction by delinquents carving rude words into them.
Big, bad, burly blokes who are a law unto themselves, dishing out indiscriminate punishment with their almighty axes.
These hooded horrors hunt their prey at night, cackling ecstatically as they wave their weapons about.
Noble knights who bounce into battle astride slimy steeds, and administer aid to ailing allies.
Didn't receive the experience bonanza you were hoping for<FH> Remember, knights shield their steeds to the bitter end<FG>
Monstrous mitts born from the blood of the executed. Let them beckon for backup, and you'll soon have a job on your hands.
It's not clear if they're masters, minions or merely mates, but stone guardians often aid them in adversity.
Burning-breathed behemoths whose hardy hides are resistant to regular attacks...save in certain specific spots.
Lizards of great longevity, they live for centuries far from civilisation in a state of peaceful repose.
Scaly soldiers whose skill with a sword is second to none. They seek out strong sparring partners to hone their art.
Their dedication to daily training makes them masters of a multitude of skills as balletic as they are brutal.
Forest-dwelling drackies who lure foes into a false sense of security, before draining them dry with Kasap.
Being a leafy shade of green, they often mistake foliage for friends, and end up talking to trees.
Crafty chests who consign booty looters to hell with a combination of speedy strikes and killer curses.
Darkness and despair lie in store for any who dare to peek beneath their lid.
Undead aristocrats who like nothing better than poking holes in proles from atop their rabid steeds.
Even in death, they take pride in their high birth, and often throw fancy feasts for their fellow blue-blooded beasts.
A myriad of minor modifications make this modern marvel of murder the most mobile on the market.
No one knows what the ‘G’ stands for, but it's more likely to be ‘Genocidal’ than ‘Gentle’.
Fiery both figuratively and factually, they let out a blood-curdling roar before flame-grilling their foes.
These walking furnaces have melted many an adventurer's arms and armour, leaving them egregiously under-equipped.
Big, beaked beasts that tear adventurers to shreds with razor-sharp talons and feast on their flesh.
They specialise in silencing enemies' spells and skills<MV>mainly because they prefer to do their murdering in peace.
Kitty cats from hell who strike fear into foes with a resounding roar before bringing their claws to bear.
Blessed with four more paws than fellow felines, they can rip and rend without ever breaking their stride.
These winged wonders use their star status to coax comrades into flinging themselves headlong into the fray.
Some say they were born in a volcano, and judging by their baking breath, that doesn't seem so hard to believe.
These cow-patterned creatures are only little, but their fierce fighting face is fit to frighten the fully grown.
With age, their black blotches gradually fade, and their pelt turns a pretty pink. But when they get older still...
Though their flesh has festered, time hasn't stripped these bare-boned battlers of their sword skills.
A brutal blow to the cranium looks to have been what sealed the fates of these once-proud paladins.
These burly bruisers are rough enough and tough enough to order regular trolls around.
They're known to make a mean human hotpot, so if these grisly gourmands lick their lips, you may be on the menu<FG>
These wily wizards prefer to fight from afar, sending foes into a flap with Sizz and Kasap.
They made monsters of themselves after falling prey to their own fascination for the arcane arts.
These cutely coloured sanguinis seem sweet until they bare their fangs, scenting the blood they need to reach adulthood.
They may seem like perfect pets, but before taking one home, you should see what they turn into...
Surly spirits of soldiers whose clogs were rudely popped. They rose again, as they still had bones to pick.
They remove their skulls and lob them<MV>not-so-living proof that losing your head in battle needn't be a bad thing.
A revenant ruler who orders his orderlies to attack adventurers while he slings spells from the sidelines.
He was never a royal in his lifetime, but rose through the ranks after death. You might call him a late, late bloomer.
These pernicious priests seek sacrifices for their depraved deity, and slyly scorch faraway foes with Sizz.
They live in harmony with other monsters, emerging from their forest homes only when their divinity demands an offering.
Sanguinis who stayed teeny when they turned into sprites. They sing a Gritty Ditty to pump up their pals in battle.
Considerate companions, they're the first to flutter over to foundering friends and proffer a helping paw.
The shades of soldiers killed in combat. Beware, however<MV> they're far more than shadows of their former selves.
Some say these shadows belonged to skeleton soldiers in life, and their cheek bones do seem strikingly similar...
These enormous effigies to a demon deity are suffused with summoned spirits, and are said to cause catastrophes.
They topple targets with tremendous tremors, and close in as their foes find their feet, sporting a stony stare.
These minor ministers to a dark deity are middling magicians...and incompetent close combatants.
Having been deprived of staffs for a lengthy spell, they prefer to keep a low profile, mixing it up with magic from afar.
Distinguished demons with rippling muscles and hellish horns, who flay foes with cruel claws and savage spells.
Their crimson complexion is a consequence of their all-consuming choler, and umpteen burst blood vessels.
A brutal beast that batters its enemies black and blue with a barbed bludgeon, smiling all the while.
Though winged, it's doomed to stay ground-bound<MV>the more it trains its flight muscles, the more mass it amasses.
A legendary lizard of epic proportions. Its brobdingnagian bulk protects it against all ordinary attacks.
Other monsters often mistake it for a mountain, and try to scale its scaly sides and plant flags in its forehead.
Nightmarish knights whose eyes shine with a ghostly glow. They sold their souls to gain supernatural strength.
One once lurked in a deserted city, guarding a sacred sword. Was he acting alone, or on the Dragonlord's orders<FH>
Rocky rogues whose grin is so engrained as to make them smile unsettlingly even when assailing adversaries.
They were volatile in their youth, but age has mellowed their mood, and they'd never consider casting Kamikazee.
These brutes boast even more brawn than their brethren, and can whip up whirling winds with a waft of their clubs.
Despite being stupidly strong, they never seem to receive the respect they deserve, and have no idea why...
Hammer-hefting halflings who psych themselves up to unleash a crushing critical hit if even slightly slighted.
They're prone to buckle under the weight of their own weapons, but they try not to let it get them down.
A four-legged fiend with teeny-weeny wings. Frightens its foes with its fangs before scratching them silly.
Some say that a child once tamed one and led it around on a lead. Needless to say, the bullies left that boy well alone.
Wicked warriors whose craving for carnage lives on in undeath, proving that homicidal habits die hard.
Though they've forgotten what they're fighting for, they don't hesitate to slay any foe foolish enough to face them.
Hell-spawned horrors who hack and hew with all four hands. Offer them an opening, and they'll cut you another one.
The sight of four grimly glinting weapons falling as if in slow motion is the last thing their victims ever see.
The leader of a northern nation whose terrifying talons serve him well as he flits and flies about the battlefield.
He's a lover of good food, and always ensures his allies' bellies are fit to burst with the finest fare.
Death droids armed with every offensive augmentation going. Their skills are a sight to behold<MV>from afar.
The product of a scientist's lifelong quest to create the perfect killer. Suffice it to say, he succeeded...
A wicked spirit recently released from a cursed lamp. Whips up whirlwinds to send foes flying.
His protracted imprisonment has made him unusually attached to his lamp, and he constantly carries it with him.
Rotten rotters rolled up in red rags. They usher their undead allies into the shadows, ready to pounce on passers-by.
Some say they were brought to life by a heretical cult, and their bandages are stained with believers' blood.
A prince among platypunks who can cast powerful spells. It ain't no Sap, but it sure can sling it.
Simple spells aren't enough for this power-hungry punk, so it trains on a daily basis to increase its magical might.
Cat-like creatures with fluffy fur, long, lolling tongues and peaceable personalities.
Candy kittens are born with a single stripe, and add another every year. Can you work out how old this one is<FH>
A ferocious feline with four front paws that fells foes with a flurry of blows, and casts hellish spells as well.
A fabled band of heroes once bested a beast of the same name, albeit in a different dimension.
This demon's powers are the envy of his fellow fiends. He pounds prey with spells before closing in for the kill.
Has served as the personal bodyguard to many a demonic despot, but in truth, finds the job hellishly stressful.
These four-armed fiends wield several different weapons at once<MV>but all with the same stunning skill.
As well as excelling at hand-to-hand combat, they can make magical mayhem with Kacrackle and Kasap.
A legend from ages past who drives foes to distraction with his searing speed and spectacular spells.
He once guarded the home of an evil priest, and fought to thwart the luminaries of the legendary line.
Ruthless robots fitted with innumerable extra enhancements, including a hover function for friction-free mobility.
Once locked-on, they employ a near-infinite range of attack patterns to ensure their target's termination.
A legendary demon general famed for condemning foes to a fiery fate with his matchless magic powers.
Like Atlas and Pazuzu, he once swore allegiance to an evil priest, and repelled the righteous with might and magic.
Eagle-eyed archers who hunt in the woods. They dip their darts in a powerful poison to fell their foes in a flash.
They're often found around bubble slimes, to whose toxic trails they turn for the venom they venerate.
Apparitions of adventurers who lost their lives, racked with regret that they failed to complete their quests.
They crave human contact, but aren't welcome anywhere, and have to make do with close-quarters combat instead.
Freshly returned from the underworld, these spirits like to scare people by popping up in front of their faces.
That they've been to hell and back makes them the envy of all their friends<MV>many are already writing their memoirs.
Eerie effigies who encourage any adventurers they encounter to join them in their danse macabre.
They were once employed by puppetmasters for entertainment purposes, but those days are long gone.
This skeletal sovereign is the commander-in-chief of an unstoppable undead army.
He is widely admired for deeply respecting the lives of others, even though he has lost his own.
Born from the burning belches of active volcanoes, they fly around the battlefield raining fire upon their foes.
Once they reach a certain size, they split into two, with both beasts sharing the same soul.
Magical manifestations of the frozen souls of spurned lovers that spew icy spells all over the place.
They'll often ambush adventurers as they emerge from the darkest dungeons, and kill them in cold blood.
Each shade is made from the shadows of many monsters who died before they could accomplish their life's work.
Having lost their identities, they shift their shapes to try and rediscover themselves. Sadly, they have little luck...
Big, bushy beasts that take it easy most of the time<MV>but if anyone attacks them, they bite right back<FG>
They do a good job of looking dozy, but are actually quite adroit. Underestimate them at your peril.
Wicked woodland warriors who usher their enemies into the hereafter with a deadly Death Dance.
They're actually very friend-focused, and dream of holding forest fetes so all their mates can dance together.
Burly bandits who love to show off their beefed-up bods before assailing adventurers with heavy hatchets.
Their families frown on their criminal careers, so they don disguises and try not to drag their names through the mud.
Dragon dragoons who wield sword and shield, and employ them to devastating effect.
A pair of these horrors once disguised themselves as humans, and guarded the hall of a heretical temple.
Cadaverous cavalrymen who ride around on demonic donkeys, impaling enemies with a needle-like lance.
To keep their bones from becoming brittle, they make sure to drink as much milk as they can manage.
Nothing escapes these trinocular tyrants' evil eyes. They terrorise travellers with speed and strength.
Their incredible eyesight gives them a bird's-eye view of the battlefield even when standing on the ground<FG>
Long-suffering spirits keen to offload their pain onto others with spells slung from a skull-topped sceptre.
They can't remember what caused their emotional imbalance, but whatever it was, only pain remains.
An avaricious alchemist who stole the Secret of Evolution and transformed himself into a monster.
He murdered his master to steal his ultimate invention<MV>little did he know that it was incomplete...
Cruel cavaliers clad in bright blue armour who overpower their enemies with monstrous might.
Some say that the armour is actually empty, but few have ever got close enough to confirm this.
A cat-like creature that plummets onto its prey from above and rends it to ribbons with its cruel claws.
Its patterned pelt is highly prized in certain circles, and sells for billions on the black market.
The cloud-bound commander of the Al-Khazami army, who leads a legion of fellow lamp-dwellers.
Had a rightly-deserved reputation as a firm but fair ruler until the Sword of Discord discombobulated him.
Carefree creatures born from clouds. They whip up whirlwinds on a whim, and fling their foes to and fro.
They spend most of their lives sitting comfortably on their clouds<MV>engaging their enemies is the only exercise they get<FG>
Creepy creatures wrapped top to toe in bandages. You can feel their fury in every thump they throw.
They carry spare bandages with them at all times to ensure they arrive at every battle looking spick and span.
Big-beaked beasts who gob blobs of sticky liquid at their enemies. Nobody's quite sure where it comes from.
They look a lot like their platypunk cousins, but can be identified by their tasteful tawny colour scheme.
Feline fiends who can fall asleep any time, anywhere, but always remain alert to approaching enemies.
An evil inventor bred them to hunt rats in his castle. Alas, cats being cats, they soon escaped and went walkabout.
Evil elfin fiends who wield a bow and arrow better than any other breed of bodkin.
Only those who have reached the apex of archery are allowed to wear the yellow hood of the bodkin bowyer.
Phantoms formed from infernal flames who attack adventurers with scorching spells.
Scholars are undecided whether they are embodiments of the Frizz spell, or the sizzling souls of the damned.
Purple poltergeists who dwell in the darkness. They're easily identified by their gaudy green headgear.
They think of themselves as sophisticated city slickers, and sneer at their country-born brethren.
A rainbow-coloured relative of the mud mannequin whose pottery body packs a serious magical punch.
It takes a long time and a carefully controlled exposure to the elements for its distinctive design to develop.
Mist-like monsters with hearts as cold as ice. They send snowstorms to obliterate their enemies.
These frosty fiends are often found atop snowy peaks, freezing off-piste explorers with their blizzard-like breath.
These shape-shifting shadows are formed from the fury-filled souls of men murdered in cold blood.
To assuage their anger, they attack any adventurer who approaches<MV>so approach at your peril.
Desert-dwelling relatives of the powie yowie whose thick fur pelts make them perspire prodigiously.
They're born with coats as icy white as other yetis, but the scorching sun soon gives them a golden glow.
A tree that took root in the underworld many millennia ago, and developed into a deciduous demon.
Some believe its leaves can grant eternal life, and pluck them from its crown, creating an ever-expanding bald spot.
These monstrous muggers are particularly persistent, pursuing their prey to the ends of the earth.
Some say their red hoods are trophies taken from little girls on their way to visit their grandmas<MV>with good reason.
Reptilian all-rounders who aren't only experts in sword and shield, but at slinging spells too.
Some say they studied sorcery under a wicked wight king in their quest to become the strongest saurian soldiers.
Hadean horsemen who ride hell-sent steeds, and condemn enemies to death with their lethal lances.
Their mounts are a magnificent maroon, and enjoy making mincemeat of any who get in their way.
Don't be fooled by its avian appearance<MV>this beast is no birdbrain. It excels at arts both martial and liberal.
It once served a demon king, stirring its fellow fiends into a frenzy with its rousing oration.
A malevolent minister who preaches at the pulpit of pain, converting his congregation to ashes with unholy hexes.
He was once a faithful servant of the Goddess, till his lust for power made him stray from the pious path.
A titanic, tree-trunk-wielding fiend that strikes terror into the hearts of even the hardiest adventurers.
One once served the Master of Monsterkind, and used wicked wiles to hoodwink the hero who was after its head.
An abandoned suit of blood-red armour infused with evil energies in order to bring it back to life.
It's far too big to fit a normal knight, but the mystery of who once wore it is one that has yet to be solved.
The biggest, baddest member of the flying feline family. It shreds its enemies without showing any remorse at all.
Its cruel claws and ferocious fangs can rip any armour to ribbons<MV>so watch out<FG>
A monstrous monarch who was sealed inside a magic lamp. He'll grant your wishes, but at a painful price.
Though he's called a ‘high’ djinks, his position in the pecking order of powerful monsters is pretty low overall.
Wearing crimson cowls and wielding golden bows, these bodkin bowmasters turn their prey into pincushions.
Some say their scarlet snoods are dyed with the blood of their enemies, while others insist it's just beetroot.
The cursed incantation Kazammle given physical form. Being made of pure magic, it can sling the strongest spells.
The foremost mages in the netherworld combined their powers to beget this being. No wonder it's so puffed-up.
The fiend who fomented the War of Kings, and brought the Seven Realms to the brink of obliteration.
He became a demon, and after biding his time for a thousand years, returned to exact his revenge.
A fire-breathing beast with shining cerulean scales. They live the longest of all the dragon family.
It's not known if they're born with blue scales, or if they change as they age<MV>nobody's ever seen a baby one.
Demonic dictators who bully other beasts with their superior strength and magical might.
When their horns drop off, it's a sign that their time is nigh, so they slip off to a secluded spot and meet their maker.
Fun-loving fiends who love nothing better than whacking away with their massive mallets.
Their dinky, inky eyes are deep enough to swim in, and blend beautifully with their jet-black bodies.
A tyrant among trolls who rules over his fellow fiends with an iron fist...and a wooden club.
They're engaged in a ceaseless struggle with their ‘stout’ cousins over who has the top spot in troll society.
War-like lizards who wield incendiary axes. Their scarlet scales are so strong, only the hardest hits can hurt them.
They've acquired a reputation as expert axemen, but actually, they just wave their weapons around willy-nilly.
After plunging the corrupted Cup of Kings into his chest, Fractos took on this ferocious final form.
Now that his strength exceeds that of the gods themselves, he plans to reduce the Seven Realms to rubble.
Buried bodies brought back to some semblance of life. Strike and slice all you like<MV>their undead flesh feels no pain.
They may be teeming with toxins, but their bodies are so rotten anyway that it doesn't make a difference.
Empty suits of armour possessed by the souls of soldiers, and fated to fight till their deaths are avenged.
The armour itself was forged in an infernal furnace<MV>rumour has it that they mass produce them in purgatory.
Half bat, half baboon, all bad. They're so aggressive, they'll attack anything they see.
Their pinkish pelts are highly prized by collectors, but all efforts to domesticate them have ended in disaster.
Rage-fuelled relatives of the hellion whose furiously flailing arms are a heck of a health hazard.
They're beastly brutes who love nothing better than ripping their enemies limb from limb. Stay well away.
The undisputed champion of the underworld. His mastery of magic and martial arts is a result of his tireless training.
He cuts a fine figure in his crimson cape<MV>a monstrous matador who makes all the other monsters say ‘olé<FG>’
A hirsute hustler who creates incorporeal copies of himself to confuse and confound his enemies.
He was once beaten black and blue by a petite princess, and dreams of the day that he can return the favour.
A dread demon who desires nothing but power, and seeks out the strongest sparring partners to perfect his art.
Was once allied with a certain Archfiend, but was bested by a worthy warrior in his flying fortress.
One of the four gruesome guardians who watch over the entrance to the throne room of the Black Manse.
His master, Fractos, keeps him hungry for human flesh, so his tummy is always rumbling.
Ferocious felines with bright white coats who pounce on passing adventurers and put them through their paces.
They blind unwary adversaries with their beauty before sealing the deal with their talons and teeth.
The Supreme Sovereign of the Seven Realms. His  benevolence has been replaced by brutal ambition.
Fractos disguised himself as the King's twin as part of his plot to trick him into annihilating humankind.
The ultimate in automatic mayhem. It draws its enemies in before annihilating them in one fell swoop.
Its inventor feared its apocalyptic power, so production never passed the prototype phase.
As Lord of the Underworld, he discovered the Secret of Evolution, and used it to become the ultimate life form.
Fearing his new-found power, the forces of good sealed him away in an endless slumber, sabres still in hand.
The terrifying true form of the doyen of dragons, whose blistering breath obliterates all who oppose him.
He often offers heroes half the world in return for their allegiance<MV>but anyone who accepts is never seen again...
